questions.stem: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum. This speed is:
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in a vacuum: c = 3 x 10^8 m/s.

questions.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelength (greater than 1 m) and lowest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength in the EM spectrum. Higher frequency means more energy per photon.

questions.stem: How many regions make up the electromagnetic spectrum?
questions.explanation: The EM spectrum has seven regions: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays.

options.text: Transverse waves that can travel through a vacuum
Longitudinal waves that can travel through a vacuum
Longitudinal waves that need a medium
Transverse waves that need a medium

questions.explanation: EM waves are transverse waves consisting of oscillating electric and magnetic fields. They do not require a medium and can travel through a vacuum.

questions.stem: In the visible light spectrum, which colour has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength (about 380-450 nm) in the visible spectrum. Red light has the longest wavelength (about 620-700 nm).

questions.stem: As you move from radio waves to gamma rays across the EM spectrum:

options.text: Both wavelength and frequency stay the same

questions.explanation: Moving from radio waves to gamma rays, wavelength decreases and frequency increases. Since v = f x lambda and speed is constant, frequency and wavelength are inversely related.
